sanskrit: tataḥ prasthāpya sugrīvas tan mahad vānaraṃ balam dakṣiṇāṃ preṣayām āsa vānarān abhilakṣitān
english: Then Sugrīva, having dispatched that great monkey army, sent to the south those monkeys distinguished by their marks.

sanskrit: nīlam agnisutaṃ caiva hanumantaṃ ca vānaram pitāmahasutaṃ caiva jāmbavantaṃ mahākapim
english: Nīla, son of Agni, and the monkey Hanūmant, and the great ape Jāmbavant, son of Pitāmaha —

sanskrit: suhotraṃ ca śarīraṃ ca śaragulmaṃ tathaiva ca gajaṃ gavākṣaṃ gavayaṃ suṣeṇam ṛṣabhaṃ tathā
english: and Suhotra, Śarīra, and Śaragulma likewise, Gaja, Gavākṣa, Gavaya, Suṣeṇa, and Ṛṣabha,

sanskrit: maindaṃ ca dvividaṃ caiva vijayaṃ gandhamādanam ulkāmukham asaṅgaṃ ca hutāśana sutāv ubhau
english: and Mainda and Dvivida, Vijaya and Gandhamādana, Ulkāmukha and Asaṅga — both sons of Hutāśana —

sanskrit: aṅgadapramukhān vīrān vīraḥ kapigaṇeśvaraḥ vegavikramasaṃpannān saṃdideśa viśeṣavit
english: these heroes led by Aṅgada — swift and valiant — the heroic lord of the monkey troops, wise in distinctions, commanded.

sanskrit: teṣām agreṣaraṃ caiva mahad balam asaṃgagam vidhāya harivīrāṇām ādiśad dakṣiṇāṃ diśam
english: Placing at their van a great and unimpeded force of monkey heroes, he directed them toward the southern quarter.

sanskrit: ye ke cana samuddeśās tasyāṃ diśi sudurgamāḥ kapīśaḥ kapimukhyānāṃ sa teṣāṃ tān udāharat
english: Whatever localities in that direction were most difficult of access, the lord of monkeys recounted them all to those foremost of monkeys.

sanskrit: sahasraśirasaṃ vindhyaṃ nānādrumalatāvṛtam narmadāṃ ca nadīṃ durgāṃ mahoraganiṣevitām
english: The Vindhya with its thousand peaks, covered with diverse trees and creepers, and the river Narmadā, difficult of passage, haunted by great serpents —

sanskrit: tato godāvarīṃ ramyāṃ kṛṣṇāveṇīṃ mahānadīm varadāṃ ca mahābhāgāṃ mahoraganiṣevitām
english: then the lovely Godāvarī, the great river Kṛṣṇāveṇī, and the auspicious Varadā, that most blessed stream haunted by great serpents —

sanskrit: mekhalān utkalāṃś caiva daśārṇanagarāṇy api avantīm abhravantīṃ ca sarvam evānupaśyata
english: the Mekhala lands and the Utkala country, the cities of Daśārṇa, and Avanti and Abhravantī — search all of these.

sanskrit: vidarbhān ṛṣikāṃś caiva ramyān māhiṣakān api tathā baṅgān kaliṅgāṃś ca kauśikāṃś ca samantataḥ
english: The Vidarbhas, the lovely Ṛṣikas, the Māhiṣakas as well, and likewise the Baṅgas, the Kaliṅgas, and the Kauśikas on all sides.

sanskrit: anvīkṣya daṇḍakāraṇyaṃ saparvatanadīguham nadīṃ godāvarīṃ caiva sarvam evānupaśyata
english: Having searched the Daṇḍaka forest with its mountains, rivers, and caves, and the river Godāvarī — inspect all of it.

sanskrit: tathaivāndhrāṃś ca puṇḍrāṃś ca colān pāṇḍyān sakeralān ayomukhaś ca gantavyaḥ parvato dhātumaṇḍitaḥ
english: Likewise the Āndhra country and the Puṇḍras, the Colas, Pāṇḍyas, and Keralas; and the mountain Ayomukha, adorned with mineral ores, must be visited.

sanskrit: vicitraśikharaḥ śrīmāṃś citrapuṣpitakānanaḥ sacandanavanoddeśo mārgitavyo mahāgiriḥ
english: That great mountain with its variegated peaks, its forests bright with flowering trees, its tracts of sandalwood groves — that splendid range must be searched.

sanskrit: tatas tām āpagāṃ divyāṃ prasannasalilāṃ śivām tatra drakṣyatha kāverīṃ vihṛtām apsarogaṇaiḥ
english: Then you shall see the divine Kāverī, that auspicious river of clear waters, where bands of Apsarases disport themselves.

sanskrit: tasyāsīnaṃ nagasyāgre malayasya mahaujasaṃ drakṣyathādityasaṃkāśam agastyam ṛṣisattamam
english: There on the crest of mount Malaya you shall see Agastya, best of seers, of mighty power and radiance like the sun, seated there.

sanskrit: tatas tenābhyanujñātāḥ prasannena mahātmanā tāmraparṇīṃ grāhajuṣṭāṃ tariṣyatha mahānadīm
english: Then, granted leave by that great-souled one in his graciousness, you shall cross the great river Tāmraparṇī, frequented by crocodiles.

sanskrit: sā candanavanair divyaiḥ pracchannā dvīpa śālinī kānteva yuvatiḥ kāntaṃ samudram avagāhate
english: Shrouded in divine groves of sandal, adorned with islands, she enters the beloved sea like a young woman embracing her beloved.

sanskrit: tato hemamayaṃ divyaṃ muktāmaṇivibhūṣitam yuktaṃ kavāṭaṃ pāṇḍyānāṃ gatā drakṣyatha vānarāḥ
english: Then, having gone there, you monkeys shall see the divine gate of the Pāṇḍyas, made of gold and adorned with pearls and gems.

sanskrit: tataḥ samudram āsādya saṃpradhāryārthaniścayam agastyenāntare tatra sāgare viniveśitaḥ
english: Then, having reached the ocean and deliberated on your purpose, you will find there in the sea what was installed by Agastya.

sanskrit: citranānānagaḥ śrīmān mahendraḥ parvatottamaḥ jātarūpamayaḥ śrīmān avagāḍho mahārṇavam
english: The splendid Mahendra, foremost of mountains, bright with diverse trees, golden and glorious, plunges into the great ocean.

sanskrit: nānāvidhair nagaiḥ phullair latābhiś copaśobhitam devarṣiyakṣapravarair apsarobhiś ca sevitam
english: It is adorned with diverse kinds of flowering trees and creepers and is frequented by foremost gods, sages, yakṣas, and Apsarases.

sanskrit: siddhacāraṇasaṃghaiś ca prakīrṇaṃ sumanoharam tam upaiti sahasrākṣaḥ sadā parvasu parvasu
english: It is scattered with throngs of Siddhas and Cāraṇas and is most enchanting; the thousand-eyed Indra always visits it on each sacred day.

sanskrit: dvīpas tasyāpare pāre śatayojanam āyataḥ agamyo mānuṣair dīptas taṃ mārgadhvaṃ samantataḥ tatra sarvātmanā sītā mārgitavyā viśeṣataḥ
english: On the further shore of it lies an island, a hundred yojanas in extent, blazing with light, inaccessible to humans — search it on all sides. There Sītā must be sought with all your might, above all.

sanskrit: sa hi deśas tu vadhyasya rāvaṇasya durātmanaḥ rākṣasādhipater vāsaḥ sahasrākṣasamadyuteḥ
english: For that region is the abode of the wicked Rāvaṇa, the lord of Rākṣasas deserving death, whose splendor equals that of the thousand-eyed Indra.

sanskrit: dakṣiṇasya samudrasya madhye tasya tu rākṣasī aṅgāraketi vikhyātā chāyām ākṣipya bhojinī
english: In the midst of that southern ocean there is a Rākṣasī known as Aṅgārakā, who feeds by seizing the shadow of her prey.

sanskrit: tam atikramya lakṣmīvān samudre śatayojane giriḥ puṣpitako nāma siddhacāraṇasevitaḥ
english: Having passed her, there is in the sea at a hundred yojanas a glorious mountain named Puṣpitaka, frequented by Siddhas and Cāraṇas.

sanskrit: candrasūryāṃśusaṃkāśaḥ sāgarāmbusamāvṛtaḥ bhrājate vipulaiḥ śṛṅgair ambaraṃ vilikhann iva
english: Radiant as the rays of the sun and moon, surrounded by the waters of the ocean, it gleams with its broad peaks as if scratching the sky.

sanskrit: tasyaikaṃ kāñcanaṃ śṛṅgaṃ sevate yaṃ divākaraḥ śvetaṃ rājatam ekaṃ ca sevate yaṃ niśākaraḥ
english: One of its peaks is golden — that one the sun frequents; one is white and silvery — that one the moon frequents.

sanskrit: na taṃ kṛtaghnāḥ paśyanti na nṛśaṃsā na nāstikāḥ praṇamya śirasā śailaṃ taṃ vimārgata vānarāḥ
english: The ungrateful do not see it, nor the cruel, nor the impious. Having bowed your heads to that mountain, search onward, O monkeys.

sanskrit: tam atikramya durdharṣāḥ sūryavān nāma parvataḥ adhvanā durvigāhena yojanāni caturdaśa
english: Having passed it, O irresistible ones, there is a mountain named Sūryavān, fourteen yojanas distant along a road difficult to traverse.

sanskrit: tatas tam apy atikramya vaidyuto nāma parvataḥ sarvakāmaphalair vṛkṣaiḥ sarvakālamanoharaiḥ
english: And having passed that too, there is the mountain named Vaidyuta, with trees bearing fruits of all desires, charming in every season.

sanskrit: tatra bhuktvā varārhāṇi mūlāni ca phalāni ca madhūni pītvā mukhyāni paraṃ gacchata vānarāḥ
english: There, having eaten the excellent roots and fruits and drunk the finest honeys, proceed onward, O monkeys.

sanskrit: tatra netramanaḥkāntaḥ kuñjaro nāma parvataḥ agastyabhavanaṃ yatra nirmitaṃ viśvakarmaṇā
english: There is a mountain named Kuñjara, delightful to eye and mind, where the dwelling of Agastya was built by Viśvakarman.

sanskrit: tatra yojanavistāram ucchritaṃ daśayojanam śaraṇaṃ kāñcanaṃ divyaṃ nānāratnavibhūṣitam
english: There stands a divine golden pavilion, one yojana wide and ten yojanas high, adorned with various jewels.

sanskrit: tatra bhogavatī nāma sarpāṇām ālayaḥ purī viśālarathyā durdharṣā sarvataḥ parirakṣitā rakṣitā pannagair ghorais tīkṣṇadaṃṣṭrair mahāviṣaiḥ
english: There is the city called Bhogavatī, abode of serpents, with broad thoroughfares, formidable, guarded on all sides, protected by dreadful serpents with sharp fangs and great venom.

sanskrit: sarparājo mahāghoro yasyāṃ vasati vāsukiḥ niryāya mārgitavyā ca sā ca bhogavatī purī
english: In it dwells Vāsuki, the great and terrible king of serpents; venturing out, that city of Bhogavatī must be searched.

sanskrit: taṃ ca deśam atikramya mahān ṛṣabhasaṃsthitaḥ sarvaratnamayaḥ śrīmān ṛṣabho nāma parvataḥ
english: Having passed that region, there stands great Ṛṣabha, shaped like a bull, the glorious mountain called Ṛṣabha, composed of all manner of gems.

sanskrit: gośīrṣakaṃ padmakaṃ ca hariśyāmaṃ ca candanam divyam utpadyate yatra tac caivāgnisamaprabham
english: There the divine sandal varieties grow: Gośīrṣaka, Padmaka, and the dark-green Hariśyāma, as brilliant as fire.

sanskrit: na tu tac candanaṃ dṛṣṭvā spraṣṭavyaṃ ca kadā cana rohitā nāma gandharvā ghorā rakṣanti tad vanam
english: Yet having seen those sandalwood trees they must never be touched, for fearsome Gandharvas named Rohitas guard that forest.

sanskrit: tatra gandharvapatayaḥ pañcasūryasamaprabhāḥ śailūṣo grāmaṇīr bhikṣuḥ śubhro babhrus tathaiva ca
english: There the lords of Gandharvas dwell, each blazing like five suns: Śailūṣa, Grāmaṇī, Bhikṣu, Śubhra, and Babhru likewise.

sanskrit: ante pṛthivyā durdharṣās tatra svargajitaḥ sthitāḥ tataḥ paraṃ na vaḥ sevyaḥ pitṛlokaḥ sudāruṇaḥ rājadhānī yamasyaiṣā kaṣṭena tamasāvṛtā
english: At the very end of the earth, those irresistible ones stand who have conquered heaven. Beyond that, you must not enter the realm of the Pitṛs — most terrible, the capital of Yama, shrouded in dreadful darkness.

sanskrit: etāvad eva yuṣmābhir vīrā vānarapuṃgavāḥ śakyaṃ vicetuṃ gantuṃ vā nāto gatimatāṃ gatiḥ
english: Only thus far, O heroes, O foremost of monkeys, is it possible for you to search and go — beyond this there is no path even for those who can move anywhere.

sanskrit: sarvam etat samālokya yac cānyad api dṛśyate gatiṃ viditvā vaidehyāḥ saṃnivartitam arhatha
english: Having surveyed all this and whatever else may be seen, and having discovered the whereabouts of the princess of Videha, you should return.

sanskrit: yas tu māsān nivṛtto 'gre dṛṣṭā sīteti vakṣyati mattulyavibhavo bhogaiḥ sukhaṃ sa vihariṣyati
english: Whoever returns within a month and declares 'Sītā has been seen' — he shall enjoy pleasures equal to mine and live in happiness.

sanskrit: tataḥ priyataro nāsti mama prāṇād viśeṣataḥ kṛtāparādho bahuśo mama bandhur bhaviṣyati
english: Furthermore, there is none dearer to me than he — above even my own life — and one who has wronged me many times shall become my kinsman.

sanskrit: amitabalaparākramā bhavanto vipulaguṇeṣu kuleṣu ca prasūtāḥ manujapatisutāṃ yathā labhadhvaṃ tad adhiguṇaṃ puruṣārtham ārabhadhvam
english: You are of immeasurable strength and valor, born in lineages of great virtue; undertake this highest of human goals so that you may find the daughter of the king of men.

sanskrit: tataḥ prasthāpya sugrīvas tān harīn dakṣiṇāṃ diśam buddhivikramasaṃpannān vāyuvegasamāñjave
english: Then Sugrīva, having dispatched those monkeys endowed with intelligence and valor — swift as the wind — to the southern direction,

sanskrit: athāhūya mahātejāḥ suṣeṇaṃ nāma yūthapam tārāyāḥ pitaraṃ rājā śvaśurabhīmavikramam
english: then summoned a troop-leader named Suṣeṇa, the mighty king, father of Tārā and his own formidably valiant father-in-law.

sanskrit: abravīt prāñjalir vākyam abhigamya praṇamya ca sāhāyyaṃ kuru rāmasya kṛtye 'smin samupasthite
english: He approached him with joined palms, bowed, and said: "Render your assistance to Rāma in this task that has now presented itself."

sanskrit: vṛtaḥ śatasahasreṇa vānarāṇāṃ tarasvinām abhigaccha diśaṃ saumya paścimāṃ vāruṇīṃ prabho
english: "Attended by a hundred thousand swift monkeys, O gentle one, O lord, proceed to the western quarter, the quarter of Varuṇa."

sanskrit: surāṣṭrān saha bāhlīkāñ śūrābhīrāṃs tathaiva ca sphītāñjanapadān ramyān vipulāni purāṇi ca
english: "The Surāṣṭra lands together with the Bāhlīkas, the Śūrābhīras likewise, the prosperous Añjana territories, their lovely settlements and great cities —"

sanskrit: puṃnāgagahanaṃ kukṣiṃ bahuloddālakākulam tathā ketakaṣaṇḍāṃś ca mārgadhvaṃ hariyūthapāḥ
english: "thickets of puṃnāga trees, regions dense with uddalāka trees, and groves of ketaka — search all these, O leaders of monkey troops."

sanskrit: pratyak srotogamāś caiva nadyaḥ śītajalāḥ śivāḥ tāpasānām araṇyāni kāntārā girayaś ca ye
english: "Rivers flowing westward with cool and auspicious waters, the forests of ascetics, the wildlands, and whatever mountains there are —"

sanskrit: girijālāvṛtāṃ durgāṃ mārgitvā paścimāṃ diśam tataḥ paścimam āsādya samudraṃ draṣṭum arhatha timi nakrāyuta jalam akṣobhyam atha vānaraḥ
english: "Having searched the west, that difficult quarter enclosed by chains of mountains, then upon reaching the western ocean you shall behold its unagitated waters teeming with timi fish and crocodiles, O monkeys."

sanskrit: tataḥ ketakaṣaṇḍeṣu tamālagahaneṣu ca kapayo vihariṣyanti nārikelavaneṣu ca
english: "Then the monkeys shall roam through groves of ketaka, through dense tamāla forests, and through coconut groves."

sanskrit: tatra sītāṃ ca mārgadhvaṃ nilayaṃ rāvaṇasya ca marīcipattanaṃ caiva ramyaṃ caiva jaṭīpuram
english: "There search for Sītā and for the dwelling of Rāvaṇa, and also the lovely city of Marīcipattana and Jaṭīpura."

sanskrit: avantīm aṅgalopāṃ ca tathā cālakṣitaṃ vanam rāṣṭrāṇi ca viśālāni pattanāni tatas tataḥ
english: "Avanti and Aṅgalopā, the unseen forest, and the broad kingdoms and towns here and there —"

sanskrit: sindhusāgarayoś caiva saṃgame tatra parvataḥ mahān hemagirir nāma śataśṛṅgo mahādrumaḥ
english: "At the confluence of the Sindhu and the ocean there is a great mountain named Hemagiri, with a hundred peaks and mighty trees."

sanskrit: tasya prastheṣu ramyeṣu siṃhāḥ pakṣagamāḥ sthitāḥ timimatsyagajāṃś caiva nīḍāny āropayanti te
english: "On its beautiful plateaus live winged lions who carry timi fish, ordinary fish, and elephants up to their nests."

sanskrit: tāni nīḍāni siṃhānāṃ giriśṛṅgagatāś ca ye dṛptās tṛptāś ca mātaṅgās toyadasvananiḥsvanāḥ vicaranti viśāle 'smiṃs toyapūrṇe samantataḥ
english: "In those nests of the lions, and on the mountain peaks, proud and well-fed elephants, rumbling like thunder-clouds, roam about through that vast water-filled expanse on all sides."

sanskrit: tasya śṛṅgaṃ divasparśaṃ kāñcanaṃ citrapādapam sarvam āśu vicetavyaṃ kapibhiḥ kāmarūpibhiḥ
english: "Its sky-touching golden peak, with its variegated trees — all of this must be swiftly searched by the shape-shifting monkeys."

sanskrit: koṭiṃ tatra samudre tu kāñcanīṃ śatayojanam durdarśāṃ pariyātrasya gatā drakṣyatha vānarāḥ
english: "There in the ocean you shall see the golden cape of Pariyātra, a hundred yojanas in extent, difficult to behold, O monkeys."

sanskrit: koṭyas tatra caturviṃśad gandharvāṇāṃ tarasvinām vasanty agninikāśānāṃ ghorāṇāṃ kāmarūpiṇām
english: "Twenty-four crores of swift Gandharvas dwell there, terrible shape-shifters blazing like fire."

sanskrit: nātyāsādayitavyās te vānarair bhīmavikramaiḥ nādeyaṃ ca phalaṃ tasmād deśāt kiṃ cit plavaṃgamaiḥ
english: "Those Gandharvas must not be approached too closely by even the formidably valiant monkeys, and no fruit whatsoever from that region must be taken by the leaping ones."

sanskrit: durāsadā hi te vīrāḥ sattvavanto mahābalāḥ phalamūlāni te tatra rakṣante bhīmavikramāḥ
english: "For those heroes are unapproachable, possessed of great vitality and might; those ones of fearsome valor guard the fruits and roots there."

sanskrit: tatra yatnaś ca kartavyo mārgitavyā ca jānakī na hi tebhyo bhayaṃ kiṃ cit kapitvam anuvartatām
english: "Yet effort must be made there and Jānakī must be sought; there is no fear at all from them for those who follow the nature of monkeys."

sanskrit: caturbhāge samudrasya cakravān nāma parvataḥ tatra cakraṃ sahasrāraṃ nirmitaṃ viśvakarmaṇā
english: "At the fourth quarter of the ocean stands the mountain named Cakravān; there the discus of a thousand spokes was fashioned by Viśvakarman."

sanskrit: tatra pañcajanaṃ hatvā hayagrīvaṃ ca dānavam ājahāra tataś cakraṃ śaṅkhaṃ ca puruṣottamaḥ
english: "There, having slain Pañcajana and the demon Hayagrīva, the Supreme Person carried off the discus and the conch shell."

sanskrit: tasya sānuṣu citreṣu viśālāsu guhāsu ca rāvaṇaḥ saha vaidehyā mārgitavyas tatas tataḥ
english: "On its variegated slopes and in its vast caves, Rāvaṇa together with the princess of Videha must be searched for here and there."

sanskrit: yojanāni catuḥṣaṣṭir varāho nāma parvataḥ suvarṇaśṛṅgaḥ suśrīmān agādhe varuṇālaye
english: "Sixty-four yojanas distant, in the fathomless realm of Varuṇa, stands the mountain named Varāha, with golden peaks, supremely splendid."

sanskrit: tatra prāgjyotiṣaṃ nāma jātarūpamayaṃ puram yasmin vasti duṣṭātmā narako nāma guhāsu ca
english: "There is the golden city called Prāgjyotiṣa, in which the evil-souled one named Naraka dwells, in caves as well."

sanskrit: tasya sānuṣu citreṣu viśālāsu guhāsu ca rāvaṇaḥ saha vaidehyā mārgitavyas tatas tataḥ
english: "On its variegated slopes and in its vast caves, Rāvaṇa together with the princess of Videha must be searched for here and there."

sanskrit: tam atikramya śailendraṃ kāñcanāntaranirdaraḥ parvataḥ sarvasauvarṇo dhārā prasravaṇāyutaḥ
english: "Having passed that king of mountains, there is a wholly golden mountain with rifts and caverns of gold within, filled with cascades and waterfalls."

sanskrit: taṃ gajāś ca varāhāś ca siṃhā vyāghrāś ca sarvataḥ abhigarjanti satataṃ tena śabdena darpitāḥ
english: "Elephants, boars, lions, and tigers continually roar all around it, made proud by that very sound."

sanskrit: tasmin harihayaḥ śrīmān mahendraḥ pākaśāsanaḥ abhiṣiktaḥ surai rājā meghavān nāma parvataḥ
english: "On that mountain named Meghavān, the splendid Mahendra with horse-colored steeds, Pākaśāsana Indra, was consecrated king by the gods."

sanskrit: tam atikramya śailendraṃ mahendraparipālitam ṣaṣṭiṃ girisahasrāṇi kāñcanāni gamiṣyatha
english: "Having passed that king of mountains guarded by Mahendra, you shall travel through sixty thousand golden peaks."

sanskrit: taruṇādityavarṇāni bhrājamānāni sarvataḥ jātarūpamayair vṛkṣaiḥ śobhitāni supuṣpitaiḥ
english: "They are the color of the young sun, gleaming on all sides, beautified by golden trees in full bloom."

sanskrit: teṣāṃ madhye sthito rājā merur uttamaparvataḥ ādityena prasannena śailo dattavaraḥ purā
english: "In the midst of these stands the king Meru, the highest of mountains — the mountain to which a boon was granted of old by the gracious Āditya."

sanskrit: tenaivam uktaḥ śailendraḥ sarva eva tvadāśrayāḥ matprasādād bhaviṣyanti divārātrau ca kāñcanāḥ
english: "Thus addressed by the sun, the lord of mountains was told: 'All those who take refuge in you shall become golden by my grace, both by day and by night.'"

sanskrit: tvayi ye cāpi vatsyanti devagandharvadānavāḥ te bhaviṣyanti raktāś ca prabhayā kāñcanaprabhāḥ
english: "'And whatever gods, Gandharvas, and Dānavas dwell upon you — they shall be suffused with golden radiance, blazing with that luster.'"

sanskrit: ādityā vasavo rudrā marutaś ca divaukasaḥ āgamya paścimāṃ saṃdhyāṃ merum uttamaparvatam
english: "The Ādityas, Vasus, Rudras, and Maruts — all the celestial beings — come at the western twilight to Meru, the highest of mountains,"

sanskrit: ādityam upatiṣṭhanti taiś ca sūryo 'bhipūjitaḥ adṛśyaḥ sarvabhūtānām astaṃ gacchati parvatam
english: "and attend upon the sun; and the sun, worshipped by them, becomes invisible to all creatures and goes to the western mountain."

sanskrit: yojanānāṃ sahasrāṇi daśatāni divākaraḥ muhūrtārdhena taṃ śīghram abhiyāti śiloccayam
english: "In half a muhūrta the day-maker swiftly traverses ten thousand yojanas to reach that rocky mass."

sanskrit: śṛṅge tasya mahad divyaṃ bhavanaṃ sūryasaṃnibham prāsādaguṇasaṃbādhaṃ vihitaṃ viśvakarmaṇā
english: "On its peak stands a great divine palace radiant as the sun, filled with the excellence of palatial halls, fashioned by Viśvakarman."

sanskrit: śobhitaṃ tarubhiś citrair nānāpakṣisamākulaiḥ niketaṃ pāśahastasya varuṇasya mahātmanaḥ
english: "Adorned with variegated trees and thronged with birds of all kinds, it is the abode of the great-souled Varuṇa, who holds the noose."

sanskrit: antarā merum astaṃ ca tālo daśaśirā mahān jātarūpamayaḥ śrīmān bhrājate citravedikaḥ
english: "Between Meru and the western mountain stands a great ten-headed palmyra tree, golden and splendid, blazing on its variegated altar-base."

sanskrit: teṣu sarveṣu durgeṣu saraḥsu ca saritsu ca rāvaṇaḥ saha vaidehyā mārgitavyas tatas tataḥ
english: "In all those fastnesses, and in the lakes and rivers as well, Rāvaṇa together with the princess of Videha must be searched for here and there."

sanskrit: yatra tiṣṭhati dharmātmā tapasā svena bhāvitaḥ merusāvarṇir ity eva khyāto vai brahmaṇā samaḥ
english: "There dwells the righteous-souled sage Merusāvarṇi, perfected by his own austerities, renowned, equal to Brahmā himself."

sanskrit: praṣṭavyo merusāvarṇir maharṣiḥ sūryasaṃnibhaḥ praṇamya śirasā bhūmau pravṛttiṃ maithilīṃ prati
english: "The great sage Merusāvarṇi, radiant as the sun, must be asked — bowing your heads to the ground — about any tidings concerning the daughter of Mithilā."

sanskrit: etāvaj jīvalokasya bhāskaro rajanīkṣaye kṛtvā vitimiraṃ sarvam astaṃ gacchati parvatam
english: "This far the sun illuminates the world of the living, and at the end of night, having dispelled all darkness, sets behind the western mountain."

sanskrit: etāvad vānaraiḥ śakyaṃ gantuṃ vānarapuṃgavāḥ abhāskaram amaryādaṃ na jānīmas tataḥ param
english: "Thus far, O foremost of monkeys, it is possible for monkeys to go; beyond this, sunless and boundless, we have no knowledge."

sanskrit: adhigamya tu vaidehīṃ nilayaṃ rāvaṇasya ca astaṃ parvatam āsādya pūrṇe māse nivartata
english: "But having found the princess of Videha and the dwelling of Rāvaṇa, and having reached the western mountain, return when the month is complete."

sanskrit: ūrdhvaṃ māsān na vastavyaṃ vasan vadhyo bhaven mama sahaiva śūro yuṣmābhiḥ śvaśuro me gamiṣyati
english: "No one may remain beyond a month — one who does so shall be condemned to death by me; together with you brave ones my father-in-law shall go."

sanskrit: śrotavyaṃ sarvam etasya bhavadbhir diṣṭa kāribhiḥ gurur eṣa mahābāhuḥ śvaśuro me mahābalaḥ
english: "All of what this one says must be heeded by you, who do as ordained; this is my guru, my long-armed, mighty father-in-law."

sanskrit: bhavantaś cāpi vikrāntāḥ pramāṇaṃ sarvakarmasu pramāṇam enaṃ saṃsthāpya paśyadhvaṃ paścimāṃ diśam
english: "And you too are heroic — authorities in all endeavors; taking him as your guide, proceed to survey the western quarter."

sanskrit: dṛṣṭāyāṃ tu narendrasyā patnyām amitatejasaḥ kṛtakṛtyā bhaviṣyāmaḥ kṛtasya pratikarmaṇā
english: "But once the wife of the king of immeasurable splendor has been found, we shall have accomplished our purpose by rendering this return service for what was done for us."

sanskrit: ato 'nyad api yat kiṃ cit kāryasyāsya hitaṃ bhavet saṃpradhārya bhavadbhiś ca deśakālārthasaṃhitam
english: "Whatever else besides this might be beneficial to this task, weigh it well — bearing in mind the place, the time, and the purpose."

sanskrit: tataḥ suṣeṇa pramukhāḥ plavaṃgamāḥ sugrīvavākyaṃ nipuṇaṃ niśamya āmantrya sarve plavagādhipaṃ te jagmur diśaṃ tāṃ varuṇābhiguptām
english: Then those leaping ones led by Suṣeṇa, having carefully heard Sugrīva's words and taken leave of the lord of the monkeys, all went to that quarter protected by Varuṇa.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃdiśya sugrīvaḥ śvaśuraṃ paścimāṃ diśam vīraṃ śatabaliṃ nāma vānaraṃ vānararṣabhaḥ
english: Then Sugrīva, that bull among monkeys, having dispatched his father-in-law to the western quarter, addressed the heroic monkey named Śatabali,

sanskrit: uvāca rājā mantrajñaḥ sarvavānarasaṃmatam vākyam ātmahitaṃ caiva rāmasya ca hitaṃ tathā
english: the king, learned in counsel, spoke words approved by all the monkeys, words that were for his own benefit and equally for Rāma's benefit.

sanskrit: vṛtaḥ śatasahasreṇa tvadvidhānāṃ vanaukasām vaivasvata sutaiḥ sārdhaṃ pratiṣṭhasva svamantribhiḥ
english: "Attended by a hundred thousand forest-dwellers of your kind, along with the sons of Vaivasvata, set forth with your own counselors."

sanskrit: diśaṃ hy udīcīṃ vikrāntāṃ himaśailāvataṃsakām sarvataḥ parimārgadhvaṃ rāmapatnīm aninditām
english: "Search the heroic northern quarter, crowned with the Himālayan range, on all sides for the blameless wife of Rāma."

sanskrit: asmin kārye vinivṛtte kṛte dāśaratheḥ priye ṛṇān muktā bhaviṣyāmaḥ kṛtārthārthavidāṃ varāḥ
english: "When this task is accomplished and the favor of the son of Daśaratha is fulfilled, we shall be freed from our debt — best of those who know the meaning of what is accomplished."

sanskrit: kṛtaṃ hi priyam asmākaṃ rāghaveṇa mahātmanā tasya cet pratikāro 'sti saphalaṃ jīvitaṃ bhavet
english: "For the great-souled Rāghava has done what is dear to us; if there is a return service for him, then life has borne fruit."

sanskrit: etāṃ buddhiṃ samāsthāya dṛśyate jānakī yathā tathā bhavadbhiḥ kartavyam asmatpriyahitaiṣibhiḥ
english: "Holding to this resolve, act in whatever way Jānakī may be found — you who seek what is dear and beneficial to us."

sanskrit: ayaṃ hi sarvabhūtānāṃ mānyas tu narasattamaḥ asmāsu cāgataprītī rāmaḥ parapuraṃjayaḥ
english: "For this Rāma, conqueror of enemy cities, is the most honored of all beings and came to us with affection."

sanskrit: imāni vanadurgāṇi nadyaḥ śailāntarāṇi ca bhavantaḥ parimārgaṃs tu buddhivikramasaṃpadā
english: "These forest fastnesses, rivers, and mountain gorges — search through them all with the fullness of your intelligence and valor."

sanskrit: tatra mlecchān pulindāṃś ca śūrasenāṃs tathaiva ca prasthālān bharatāṃś caiva kurūṃś ca saha madrakaiḥ
english: "There search among the Mlecchas and Pulindas, likewise the Śūrasenas, the Prasthālas and Bharatas, the Kurus along with the Madras,"

sanskrit: kāmbojān yavanāṃś caiva śakān āraṭṭakān api bāhlīkān ṛṣikāṃś caiva pauravān atha ṭaṅkaṇān
english: "the Kāmbojas and Yavanas as well, the Śakas and the Āraṭṭakas, the Bāhlīkas and Ṛṣikas, and also the Pauravans and Ṭaṅkaṇas;"

sanskrit: cīnān paramacīnāṃś ca nīhārāṃś ca punaḥ punaḥ anviṣya daradāṃś caiva himavantaṃ vicinvatha
english: "the Cīnas and Paramacīnas, and the Nīhāras again and again, and having searched the Daradas as well, thoroughly comb the Himavat mountains."

sanskrit: lodhrapadmakaṣaṇḍeṣu devadāruvaneṣu ca rāvaṇaḥ saha vaidehya mārgitavyas tatas tataḥ
english: "In the groves of lodhra and padmaka trees, and in the deodar forests, Rāvaṇa together with the princess of Videha must be sought here and there."

sanskrit: tataḥ somāśramaṃ gatvā devagandharvasevitam kālaṃ nāma mahāsānuṃ parvataṃ taṃ gamiṣyatha
english: "Then, having gone to the hermitage of Soma frequented by gods and Gandharvas, you shall proceed to that great-plateaued mountain named Kāla."

sanskrit: mahatsu tasya śṛṅgeṣu nirdareṣu guhāsu ca vicinudhvaṃ mahābhāgāṃ rāmapatnīṃ yaśasvinīm
english: "On its great peaks, in its rifts and caves, thoroughly search for the glorious, illustrious wife of Rāma."

sanskrit: tam atikramya śailendraṃ hemavargaṃ mahāgirim tataḥ sudarśanaṃ nāma parvataṃ gantum arhatha
english: "Having passed that king of mountains, the great golden Hemavarga range, you should then proceed to the mountain named Sudarśana."

sanskrit: tasya kānanaṣaṇḍeṣu nirdareṣu guhāsu ca rāvaṇaḥ saha vaidehyā mārgitavyas tatas tataḥ
english: "In its forest groves, rifts, and caves, Rāvaṇa together with the princess of Videha must be sought here and there."

sanskrit: tam atikramya cākāśaṃ sarvataḥ śatayojanam aparvatanadī vṛkṣaṃ sarvasattvavivarjitam
english: "Having passed it, there is a void sky of a hundred yojanas on all sides, without mountain, river, or tree, devoid of all living beings."

sanskrit: taṃ tu śīghram atikramya kāntāraṃ romaharṣaṇam kailāsaṃ pāṇḍuraṃ śailaṃ prāpya hṛṣṭā bhaviṣyatha
english: "But having swiftly passed that hair-raising wilderness, upon reaching the white mountain Kailāsa you shall be filled with joy."

sanskrit: tatra pāṇḍurameghābhaṃ jāmbūnadapariṣkṛtam kuberabhavanaṃ divyaṃ nirmitaṃ viśvakarmaṇā
english: "There is the divine palace of Kubera, fashioned by Viśvakarman, white as a cloud, adorned with Jāmbūnada gold."

sanskrit: viśālā nalinī yatra prabhūtakamalotpalā haṃsakāraṇḍavākīrṇā apsarogaṇasevitā
english: "There is the vast lotus pond, rich in lotuses and blue water-lilies, thronged with haṃsa and kāraṇḍava birds, frequented by bands of Apsarases."

sanskrit: tatra vaiśravaṇo rājā sarvabhūtanamaskṛtaḥ dhanado ramate śrīmān guhyakaiḥ saha yakṣarāṭ
english: "There the glorious Vaiśravaṇa, king of yakṣas, the lord of wealth honored by all beings, disports himself together with the Guhyakas."

sanskrit: tasya candranikaśeṣu parvateṣu guhāsu ca rāvaṇaḥ saha vaidehyā mārgitavyas tatas tataḥ
english: "On those moonlit mountains and in their caves, Rāvaṇa together with the princess of Videha must be sought here and there."

sanskrit: krauñcaṃ tu girim āsādya bilaṃ tasya sudurgamam apramattaiḥ praveṣṭavyaṃ duṣpraveśaṃ hi tat smṛtam
english: "Upon reaching mount Krauñca, its cave most difficult of access must be entered with utmost vigilance, for that passage is known to be hard to enter."

sanskrit: vasanti hi mahātmānas tatra sūryasamaprabhāḥ devair apy arcitāḥ samyag devarūpā maharṣayaḥ
english: "For there dwell great-souled great sages, radiant as the sun, duly worshipped even by the gods, divine in form."

sanskrit: krauñcasya tu guhāś cānyāḥ sānūni śikharāṇi ca nirdarāś ca nitambāś ca vicetavyās tatas tataḥ
english: "The other caves of Krauñca too, its plateaus, peaks, rifts, and slopes — all must be searched here and there."

sanskrit: krauñcasya śikharaṃ cāpi nirīkṣya ca tatas tataḥ avṛkṣaṃ kāmaśailaṃ ca mānasaṃ vihagālayam
english: "Having surveyed Krauñca's peak as well, here and there, then proceed to the treeless Kāmaśaila and to Mānasa, the abode of birds."

sanskrit: na gatis tatra bhūtānāṃ devadānavarakṣasām sa ca sarvair vicetavyaḥ sasānuprasthabhūdharaḥ
english: "No beings — gods, Dānavas, or Rākṣasas — have passage there; yet it must be searched by all of you, with its slopes, plateaus, and mountain heights."

sanskrit: krauñcaṃ girim atikramya maināko nāma parvataḥ mayasya bhavanaṃ tatra dānavasya svayaṃ kṛtam
english: "Having passed mount Krauñca, there is a mountain named Maināka; there is the self-built dwelling of the Dānava Maya."

sanskrit: mainākas tu vicetavyaḥ sasānuprasthakandaraḥ strīṇām aśvamukhīnāṃ ca niketās tatra tatra tu
english: "Maināka must be searched along with its slopes, plateaus, and gorges; and there here and there are the abodes of horse-faced women."

sanskrit: taṃ deśaṃ samatikramya āśramaṃ siddhasevitam siddhā vaikhānasās tatra vālakhilyāś ca tāpasāḥ
english: "Having fully passed that region, there is a hermitage frequented by Siddhas; there the Siddhas, the Vaikhānasas, and the Vālakhilya ascetics dwell."

sanskrit: vandyās te tu tapaḥsiddhās tāpasā vītakalmaṣāḥ praṣṭavyāś cāpi sītāyāḥ pravṛttaṃ vinayānvitaiḥ
english: "Those ascetics perfected through austerities, free from all blemish, must be reverenced; and with all humility they must be asked for news of Sītā."

sanskrit: hemapuṣkarasaṃchannaṃ tatra vaikhānasaṃ saraḥ taruṇādityasaṃkāśair haṃsair vicaritaṃ śubhaiḥ
english: "There is the Vaikhānasa lake, covered with golden lotuses, roamed by auspicious haṃsas radiant as the young sun."

sanskrit: aupavāhyaḥ kuberasya sarvabhauma iti smṛtaḥ gajaḥ paryeti taṃ deśaṃ sadā saha kareṇubhiḥ
english: "Kubera's riding elephant, known as Sarvabhauma, continually roams that region together with the she-elephants."

sanskrit: tat sāraḥ samatikramya naṣṭacandradivākaram anakṣatragaṇaṃ vyoma niṣpayodam anādimat
english: "Having fully passed that lake, there is a sky where moon and sun are lost, without a host of stars, cloudless, without beginning."

sanskrit: gabhastibhir ivārkasya sa tu deśaḥ prakāśate viśrāmyadbhis tapaḥ siddhair devakalpaiḥ svayamprabhaiḥ
english: "Yet that region is illuminated as if by the sun's own rays by the self-luminous ones, god-like beings perfected in austerity who rest there."

sanskrit: taṃ tu deśam atikramya śailodā nāma nimnagā ubhayos tīrayor yasyāḥ kīcakā nāma veṇavaḥ
english: "Having passed that region, there is a river named Śailodā, on both banks of which grow bamboos called Kīcaka."

sanskrit: te nayanti paraṃ tīraṃ siddhān pratyānayanti ca uttarāḥ kuravas tatra kṛtapuṇyapratiśriyāḥ
english: "Those bamboos carry the Siddhas to the far shore and bring them back again; the Uttara Kurus are there, dwelling in the reward of their accumulated merit."

sanskrit: tataḥ kāñcanapadmābhiḥ padminībhiḥ kṛtodakāḥ nīlavaidūryapatrāḍhyā nadyas tatra sahasraśaḥ
english: "Then thousands of rivers there have their waters set with golden lotuses, their leaves rich in blue vaidūrya gems."

sanskrit: raktotpalavanaiś cātra maṇḍitāś ca hiraṇmayaiḥ taruṇādityasadṛśair bhānti tatra jalāśayāḥ
english: "And the water bodies there, adorned with groves of red water-lilies and made of gold, blaze like the young sun."

sanskrit: mahārhamaṇipatraiś ca kāñcanaprabha kesaraiḥ nīlotpalavanaiś citraiḥ sa deśaḥ sarvatovṛtaḥ
english: "With leaves of most precious gems, with filaments of golden luster, with varied groves of blue lotus — that region is enclosed on all sides."

sanskrit: nistulābhiś ca muktābhir maṇibhiś ca mahādhanaiḥ udbhūtapulinās tatra jātarūpaiś ca nimnagāḥ
english: "With incomparable pearls and gems of great worth, the rivers there have banks rising up, and golden sandbars."

sanskrit: sarvaratnamayaiś citraiś avagāḍhā nagottamaiḥ jātarūpamayaiś cāpi hutāśanasamaprabhaiḥ
english: "Those best of mountains, made of all jewels and variegated, plunge deep into the waters, and golden ones blazing like fire as well."

sanskrit: nityapuṣpaphalāś cātra nagāḥ patrarathākulāḥ divyagandharasasparśāḥ sarvakāmān sravanti ca
english: "And here the trees always bear flowers and fruits, thronged with birds, divine in fragrance and taste and touch, and stream forth all desires."

sanskrit: nānākārāṇi vāsāṃsi phalanty anye nagottamāḥ muktāvaidūryacitrāṇi bhūṣaṇāni tathaiva ca
english: "Other foremost trees yield garments of various kinds, and ornaments variegated with pearls and vaidūrya likewise."

sanskrit: strīṇāṃ yāny anurūpāṇi puruṣāṇāṃ tathaiva ca sarvartusukhasevyāni phalanty anye nagottamāḥ
english: "Other foremost trees yield what is fitting for women and for men alike — things pleasant to enjoy in every season."

sanskrit: mahārhāṇi vicitrāṇi haimāny anye nagottamāḥ śayanāni prasūyante citrāstāraṇavanti ca
english: "Other foremost trees produce beds of great worth, variegated and golden, with their variously spread coverings."

sanskrit: manaḥkāntāni mālyāni phalanty atrāpare drumāḥ pānāni ca mahārhāṇi bhakṣyāṇi vividhāni ca
english: "Other trees here bear garlands delightful to the mind, and most precious drinks, and various foods as well."

sanskrit: striyaś ca guṇasaṃpannā rūpayauvanalakṣitāḥ gandharvāḥ kiṃnarā siddhā nāgā vidyādharās tathā ramante sahitās tatra nārībhir bhāskaraprabhāḥ
english: "And women endowed with virtues, marked by beauty and youth — Gandharvas, Kiṃnaras, Siddhas, Nāgas, and Vidyādharas as well, blazing as the sun, disport themselves there together with those women."

sanskrit: sarve sukṛtakarmāṇaḥ sarve ratiparāyaṇāḥ sarve kāmārthasahitā vasanti saha yoṣitaḥ
english: "All of them have performed meritorious deeds, all are devoted to pleasure, all dwell with their women together with love and prosperity."

sanskrit: gītavāditranirghoṣaḥ sotkṛṣṭahasitasvanaḥ śrūyate satataṃ tatra sarvabhūtamanoharaḥ
english: "The sound of song and music mingled with loud laughter is continually heard there, captivating the minds of all beings."

sanskrit: tatra nāmuditaḥ kaś cin nāsti kaś cid asatpriyaḥ ahany ahani vardhante guṇās tatra manoramāḥ
english: "There no one is joyless, no one has an unwelcome beloved; the charming virtues there increase day by day."

sanskrit: samatikramya taṃ deśam uttaras toyasāṃ nidhiḥ tatra somagirir nāma madhye hemamayo mahān
english: "Having fully passed that region, there is the northern treasury of waters; in its midst stands the great golden mountain named Somagiri."

sanskrit: indralokagatā ye ca brahmalokagatāś ca ye devās taṃ samavekṣante girirājaṃ divaṃ gatam
english: "Both those gods who have gone to Indra's realm and those who have gone to Brahmā's realm gaze upon that king of mountains, which has reached the sky."

sanskrit: sa tu deśo visūryo 'pi tasya bhāsā prakāśate sūryalakṣmyābhivijñeyas tapaseva vivasvatā
english: "That region, though sunless, is illuminated by its own radiance; it is recognizable by the splendor of the sun — as if by the austerity-light of the sun-god himself."

sanskrit: bhagavān api viśvātmā śambhur ekādaśātmakaḥ brahmā vasati deveśo brahmarṣiparivāritaḥ
english: "There too dwells the blessed Śambhu, the soul of the universe, of eleven forms, Brahmā the lord of gods, surrounded by Brahmarṣis."

sanskrit: na kathaṃ cana gantavyaṃ kurūṇām uttareṇa vaḥ anyeṣām api bhūtānāṃ nātikrāmati vai gatiḥ
english: "In no way must you proceed to the north of the Kurus; the passage of other beings too does not transgress beyond."

sanskrit: sā hi somagirir nāma devānām api durgamaḥ tam ālokya tataḥ kṣipram upāvartitum arhatha
english: "For Somagiri is difficult of access even to the gods; having beheld it, you should swiftly turn back from there."

sanskrit: etāvad vānaraiḥ śakyaṃ gantuṃ vānarapuṃgavāḥ abhāskaram amaryādaṃ na jānīmas tataḥ param
english: "Thus far, O foremost of monkeys, it is possible for monkeys to go; beyond this, sunless and boundless, we have no knowledge."

sanskrit: sarvam etad vicetavyaṃ yan mayā parikīrtitam yad anyad api noktaṃ ca tatrāpi kriyatāṃ matiḥ
english: "All that I have described must be searched; and what has not been mentioned — let your minds apply themselves to that as well."

sanskrit: tataḥ kṛtaṃ dāśarather mahat priyaṃ mahattaraṃ cāpi tato mama priyam kṛtaṃ bhaviṣyaty anilānalopamā videhajā darśanajena karmaṇā
english: "Then a great favor to the son of Daśaratha will have been accomplished, and a still greater one to me will have been done by that act of finding her — the daughter of Videha, unrivaled as the wind."

sanskrit: tataḥ kṛtārthāḥ sahitāḥ sabāndhavā mayārcitāḥ sarvaguṇair manoramaiḥ cariṣyathorvīṃ pratiśāntaśatravaḥ sahapriyā bhūtadharāḥ plavaṃgamāḥ
english: "Then, having accomplished your purpose, assembled with your kinsmen, honored by me, charming with all virtues, with your enemies pacified, with your beloved ones, O leaping ones who uphold existence, you shall roam the earth."
